features.text: The patient is 86 years old and male.
The patient is undergoing a follow-up after shunt surgery for hydrocephalus.
The patient has improved balance, able to walk to the dining room without help, though still requires occasional assistance from his daughter.
The patient has not experienced headaches or dizziness since the surgery.
The patient reports improved cognitive function, including better memory and the ability to engage in normal conversations.
The patient has not experienced any recent falls or significant difficulty with activities of daily living.
The patient scored 26 out of 30 on spelling and 25 out of 30 on calculations in a memory test, which is an improvement from before the surgery.
The patient's gait score was between 6 to 8 out of 12 and balance score was 12 out of 16, for a total of 18 to 20 out of 28, which is an improvement from before the surgery.
The patient has some trouble with walking, particularly with coordination, especially during the finger-to-nose test.
The patient's most recent neurological assessments used the Tinetti assessment tool for gait and balance and the MMSE for cognitive function.
The patient's most recent neurological assessments were performed after his shunt surgery in August, though the exact date was not mentioned.
The patient experiences some instability when walking, particularly when turning or walking on uneven surfaces.
The patient's memory is better than before the surgery, and he can engage in conversations without feeling lost.
The patient's blood pressure is 124/80 mmHg, heart rate is 64 bpm, and he does not have a temperature or oxygen saturation mentioned.
The patient does not have weakness, numbness, changes in vision, or speech issues.
The patient has some trouble with balance and walking but no other neurological symptoms.
The patient has not experienced any new symptoms or changes in his condition since his last visit, including no new confusion, coordination issues, headaches, or dizziness.
The patient has not noticed any significant changes in mood or emotional well-being since the surgery, feeling more stable and less confused.
The patient has not noticed any significant changes in appetite or sleep patterns since the surgery.
The patient has no additional concerns or information to share about his recovery.
